summary.intent: Work through the multi-lane NEXT-WORK plan for the callisto release tool (cleanup, test debt, SYS-RETRY, refactors, SYS-NAPI, hardening items), then migrate schemars and sort out PR stacking and merge conflicts.
summary.outcome: Opened roughly a dozen-plus PRs (#202-#208, #274-#287 range), each with local `just ci` green: fixed SYS-RETRY, added tests, refreshed docs, split init.rs/derive.rs, fixed SYS-NAPI, and migrated schemars to 1.x. Closed a wrongly opened plan PR (#201), rebased conflicting PRs and stacked #279/#280; edition-2024 PR #283 still conflicts and A2 is undecided.

repo: Tracking/handoff plans (NEXT-WORK.md) are local only: they live in .claude/plans/ and are excluded via .git/info/exclude, never committed or put in a PR.
`just ci` is the gate; the background wrapper's 'exit code 0' is unreliable, so read the log's own `exit=` line (several runs showed exit=1 from fmt-check despite a wrapper exit 0).
AGENTS.md says to use no session link in commits or PRs; commits are signed.
docs/errors.md carries a total error-code count, so every PR adding an E-code row conflicts with the others and needs rebasing after each merge.
Release harness fakes git/gh/cargo/registry; the harness log now records read-only calls, so no-op assertions compare mutating calls only.

SYS-RETRY fix: a package tagged at HEAD now has all operations (registry, tag, GitHub release) observed and stays selected until satisfied; a tag on an older commit settles without contacting providers.
Reports (status, version, snapshot, matrix) now use `ecosystem/name` ids and schemaVersion 2; `add` and `matrix --package` require the qualified form (E317 for bare).
schemars 1.x emits JSON Schema 2020-12 with `$defs` and `const`; wire types read via try_from must derive JsonSchema.
Generated matrix workflow template must be portable to macOS bash (no `mapfile`).
Dependabot #275 failed only because of the schemars major bump.
workflow: Write the failing black-box test first and prove tests fail via mutation (e.g. drop a persist, reorder steps) before trusting a passing test.
For refactors, commit characterization snapshots first, then do move-only changes and require the snapshots to pass unchanged.
Check pairwise merge conflicts across open PR branches before opening a batch; stack PRs that genuinely edit the same function via `gh stack`.
Get an independent review agent for risky changes like #202; it found a signed/multi-paragraph tag problem and a dependent-tagged-with-untagged-dependency case.
The sandbox blocks inline env commands, heredocs, cargo registry writes, GPG signing and network for gh; use script files or run those steps outside the sandbox.
A plain `git push` can silently do nothing when the local branch name differs from the remote; push explicitly.

friction: Wrongly opened the local tracking plan as PR #201 and had to close it and relocate the file.
Sandbox restrictions repeatedly forced workarounds (heredocs, inline scripts, signing, cargo cache, gh TLS, uv lock tests).
Background-task 'exit code 0' notices masked real CI failures from fmt-check.
PRs were branched off main in parallel without checking overlap, causing merge conflicts on errors.md, status.rs and the edition PR.

Could not edit the shared checkout's plan file from a background worktree session.
The existing `parse_changeset` fuzz target had not compiled for a long time.
